body: Selecting a gridmap for the first time will have an excess indicator at zero coordinates cell: (gridmap is hidden again)

Good morning, very nice to see progress on this! that's going to be so useful 🚀 Here is my feedback: - the limit of showing origins only within a specifc radius (`editors/grid_map/cell_origin_cursor_area`) is just for minimizing the rendering time. To have it at 1 by default is very confusing for the user and makes it difficult to understand what these dots mean. We probably want to increase the default to something like 100 for instance, so that we still optimise the rendering, but nothing on screen flickers/appear/disappear in most zoom levels. - the settings should either be in a right panel in the bottom panel (e.g. tool settings I suggested in other PRs), or in the gridmap settings - Selection is not blue when I change `editors/grid_map/cell_origin_cursor_area` to 100 - related to #116846, in on-grid snapping workflow (center x,y,z=false), maybe the cursor should highlight the four corners, and the selection should include the origins sitting on the edges. Or maybe the cursor should have a different shape in that workflow, so that it is obvious we select just one point. This would make sense for eyedrop and delete tool as well. But that's out of scope for this PR. - currently `editors/grid_map/cell_origin_cursor_area` seems to count the number of origins rather than the grid distance: ![cursor-distance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acb8008c-d2f0-416b-90ae-75c361b16895) Might be a minor issue, or might be significant if we try to show origins within a 100 unit radius. - can we try the dots without a contour line, or maybe a white contour, or thicker contour, or anti-aliasing contour. Here are examples of contour lines to try. The "darker" option may be a good one if we can't use anti-aliasing. EDIT: I added more thoughts on the "center x,y,z=false" workflow.
For the appearance, I prefer something like the "darker" option or no outline. Making them higher contrast makes them add way too much noise to the scene IMO.

> To have it at 1 by default is very confusing for the user and makes it difficult to understand what these dots mean. We probably want to increase the default to something like 100 for instance

I'm fine with increasing it a little, but that is **way** too much! It would just create visual pollution, specially on busy `GridMap`s.

> the settings should either be in a right panel in the bottom panel (e.g. tool settings I suggested in other PRs), or in the gridmap settings

I can add UI elements to edit those settings from the `GridMap` editor, sure.

> Selection is not blue when I change `editors/grid_map/cell_origin_cursor_area` to 100

The "nearby-the-cursor" indicators take priority over the selected ones.

> in on-grid snapping workflow (center x,y,z=false), maybe the cursor should highlight the four corners, and the selection should include the origins sitting on the edges.

Once again, way too much visual pollution. Especially since you're suggesting to increase the default distance. Also, as we talked in the dev chat, those options don't mean "on-grid snapping", as snapping to the grid is what it always does no matter what. They just make so that the mesh's origin is the top-left of the cell, instead of the middle.

> currently `editors/grid_map/cell_origin_cursor_area` seems to count the number of origins rather than the grid distance

What is happening in that GIF is correct behavior. It has a distance of one, so it shows the origins above and below it.

> can we try the dots without a contour line, or maybe a white contour, or thicker contour, or anti-aliasing contour.

I can try the "Darker" variation.

Update:
- Set default number of origins around the cursor from 1 to 3.
- Settings added to the `GridMap` editor's settings dialog.
- Make origin borders lighter.

> I'm fine with increasing it a little, but that is way too much! It would just create visual pollution, specially on busy GridMaps.

I think the origins overlay should be off by default with a visible, discoverable button in the UI to toggle it. The fact that it is busy is not necessary pollution, a lot of debug overlays are showing their info for all objects on screen for instance.

On the other hand, objects appearing and disappearing (i.e. flickering) are very distracting, and is a pollution (i.e. not informative).

We probably need more people's opinions to decide on the default visibility radius 😺 

> The "nearby-the-cursor" indicators take priority over the selected ones.

You say that as if it was intented behaviour but I don't see a use case...? As far as I understand, we want to see what we are selecting. The visibility radius clips what we see, but the color depends on the status: default, highlighted, selected.

> Once again, way too much visual pollution.

This feature is about showing the origins of cells, so yes, they can be a lot of them on screen. I don't think we should be too worried about it as the user is given control to turn it on/off and decrease the radius. The point of my feedback was that what is being highlighted, or selected, needs to be intuitive. 

> Also, as we talked in the dev chat, those options don't mean "on-grid snapping", as snapping to the grid is what it always does no matter what. They just make so that the mesh's origin is the top-left of the cell, instead of the middle.

Visually, either your origin snaps on the center of the cells (center x,y,z = true) or your origin snaps on the intersection points of the grid (center x,yz = false). This means that the selection cursor's box feels intuitive for the former, but does not feel intuitive for the latter. The cursor might need to be of a different shape when center x,yz = false. But that might be out of scope for this PR.

Finally had some time to play around with this. Functionally it does what is asked for and seems to work well, feedback above not withstanding. I'm trying to wrap my head around the actual goal here, Yes I can see the origins of the meshes added to the cells but it gets confusing quick: Sure I can see the centers of my meshes here, and its relatively clear due to the way these tiles are organised with the dots in the center of each tile, but thats because the tiles are 2x2 cells in this case. But it took me a minute to figure out the dots related to the walls. For a 1x1 cell the dots will be in the corner, but depending on orientation, it will be hard to tell which dot belongs to which mesh. Also in this screenshot, there is no way to tell which cell my 2x2 tile actually belong to, so I am wondering if we're actually solving the right thing here? But if others find this useful and informative, then I'm happy with the implementation.

> Also in this screenshot, there is no way to tell which cell my 2x2 tile actually belong to, so I am wondering if we're actually solving the right thing here?

In that mode (center x,y,z=false), the assets are visually snapped on the grid intersection rather than the cell's center. If we change the cursor to be some sort of an arrow rather than a cube in that mode, it would probably remove the confusion. 

As mentioned in a previous comment, the same confusion happens when using the selection cursor. As it is a cube we expect the 4 corners to be highlighted, but only only one corner is highlighted/selected. We would need an arrow to make it obvious we only select one intersection.

To be honest, this is the whole mode (center x,y,z=false) that is not well supported. I have been discussing it in other PRs as well. Might be worth making a proposal that covers all the little adaptions needed to make it work better.

> I am wondering if we're actually solving the right thing here?

Considering the Proposal describes the problem as

> It is usually not possible to tell which cell each mesh belongs to

And you concluded that 

> there is no way to tell which cell my 2x2 tile actually belong to

I'd say this doesn't really address the issue.

---

I have one idea to properly address this (disconsidering deeper refactoring to allow finding cells based on raycasts and collisions). The proposal suggests, among other points:
> Display a dot in the cell with the mesh

But the problem is that, in the context of meshes that aren't entirely enclosed in the cell size, a cell A doesn't know it is being occupied by a mesh painted in another cell B.

Thus, I suggest a new "occupancy"/"presence" concept: each mesh gets an optional Vector3i Array representing which neighboring cells it also occupies. If not set, behavior is the same as it currently is. If set as empty, the occupied cells would be chosen based on the mesh's `AABB` compared to the `GridMap`'s cell_size.

As an example, when a cell B is painted:
1) Given the ID, check custom data:
  If it doesn't exist, stop painting.
  If it exists, grab the occupancy Vector3i array and continue to step 2.
2) Given painted cell's orientation and step 1 data, store, in an independent map, information about which cells should be occupied around B.
  _Somehow_ these occupied cells should be specifically tied to the position B. Maybe with [custom data per cell](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/94282)?

Thus, `GridMap` will know that cell A is being occupied by a mesh painted on cell B.
Then it's a matter of making the operations of Erase, Pick etc. also check on this other map instead of going "no cell under cursor, no action taken". 
Depending on new options, Painting/Filling could be denied if the cell under cursor is occupied.

It would add a lot more data and bookkeeping though.
